newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Aug retail sales fell 10-17 pct - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Aug retail sales fell 10-17 pct - report.

text.p: Argentina's largest retail lobby groups said sales fell in August between 10 and 17 percent as a result of the uncertainty over the government's austerity measures, La Nacion reported Friday.
According to Silvio Macchiavello, vice-president of the powerful Argentine Chamber of Commerce, "sales fell between 10 and 15 percent because of uncertainty over the government's announcements."

Osvaldo Cornide of the CAME, which groups hundreds of small businesses from around the country, said the drop in sales began after former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo announced he would seek to tax widely-used food vouchers. "Sales fell between 10 and 17 percent," he said.

Ovidio Bolo, of the Argentine Chamber of Supermarkets, agreed with Cornide that the taxing of luncheon tickets has significantly harmed sales as transactions with the vouchers used by over two million persons fell by 50 percent in supermarkets.
"It is normal that in times of transition you will have uncertainty. But the government has got to stop changing the tax system all the time because that hurts us all."

New Economy Minister Roque Fernandez announced three weeks ago a set of austerity measures that included a hike in the price of fuel, the extension of VAT to a number of services and the elimination of subsidies.
But the package is constantly undergoing modifications, with lawmakers and the government negotiating concessions.
The result is that companies still do not know how they will be taxed, a situation that analysts say is discouraging sales and investments.
